findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The version-gated interpolation fix looks right. `config-path` is expanded only on v2.1 and later, `base-path` is kept across v2, and a failed version lookup stops the hook with a warning instead of guessing. The real-linter test is discriminating: on v2.0 it checks that the hook's output matches native output, and on newer versions it independently requires the forbidden-import finding. An adapter that expanded `config-path` on every version would fail it. Several other points hold up: the config search order matches golangci-lint's (cwd, then the path argument's ancestors, then home); the file-extension order matches Viper's; case-insensitive keys, legacy octals, aliases and non-JSON values are rejected safely; temporary files are created exclusively (`wx`) and cleaned up even if `cleanup` runs twice; and the outside-root symlink check uses resolved real paths. The remaining issues are edge-case fidelity gaps that either fail loudly or change outputs outside the hook's own claim. None blocks release.

go-lint/config.ts normalizeReports: only the `text` format is redirected and captured. If the customer config sends another format (json, sarif, checkstyle) to `stdout`, that output is mixed into `checked.stdout`. The mixture is then shown to the agent as `errors` and written into the customer's text report. Consider redirecting other stdout/stderr formats away from stdout, or rejecting them.

go-lint/config.ts normalizeReports and commands/go-lint.ts saveTextReport: report paths are made absolute on purpose, so every post-edit hook run overwrites the customer's configured report files (text, json, etc.) with results for a single package. When the run fails with no stdout, the text report is replaced with an empty line. Teams that point these paths at CI artifacts will silently get truncated reports.

go-lint/config.ts prepareGoLintConfig: the temporary config is written into `base`, and the process cwd becomes the package directory. Settings that golangci-lint resolves relative to the config file's directory or the process cwd now resolve elsewhere. Examples: `linters.settings.custom.*.path` plugin paths in wd/gitroot/gomod modes, and `issues.new-from-patch`. These are not normalized. They most likely fail loudly rather than silently, but the effective policy can still differ from a native run.

commands/go-lint.ts configPathInterpolation: the version lookup runs even in `--no-config` mode and when the config contains no placeholders. A golangci-lint build whose `version --short` output doesn't match `^v?\d+\.\d+\.` (for example `(devel)`) therefore disables linting and formatting entirely. Consider resolving the version only when a placeholder is actually present.
commands/go-lint.ts: when `run` exits non-zero with empty stdout, its stderr is pushed twice: once through `failure('run', ...)` and again through `if (checked.stderr) warnings.push(...)`.

go-lint/config.ts normalizeGocritic: `ruleguard.rules` entries go through `replace` twice (once via `mapStrings`, then again via `absolute`). This is harmless unless an expanded path itself contains a literal placeholder string, but it is unnecessary.

tests/hooks/lint-go-context.test.ts: the whole real-linter suite is skipped when Go or golangci-lint is missing, unless `SAFEWORD_REQUIRE_GO_LINT=1` is set. The ticket's claim that the test runs on every version in the matrix depends on CI setting that variable for each lane, and the CI config was not in this packet.
